title: Taser study on the right track
article: The new study of the Tasers used by B.C. police departments includes some welcome recommendations.
The study, headed by Victoria Police Chief Paul Battershill, says police should hang onto the weapons, but departments need to train officers better and track the use of Tasers more thoroughly.

Police Complaint Commissioner Dirk Ryneveld ordered the study after the death of Robert Bagnell, who died after being shot by a Taser in Vancouver. Critics say that Bagnell's death and others linked to Tasers are unacceptable. Certainly, we need to do everything possible to avoid such loss of life, but police officers need a weapon that will stop an aggressive suspect without killing him.

The study looked at 4,500 uses of Tasers in North America and Europe. Only four of those were connected with deaths. That is a tiny number compared to the number of deaths of suspects, officers or civilians that would occur if the only options were hand-to-hand fighting and firearms.

The study's authors are right to call for provincewide standards in the use of Tasers. The Justice Institute, which trains police officers, is the obvious agency to ensure all B.C. officers are trained to an acceptable standard.
The study also wants to see all uses of Tasers tracked. This is an important step in finding and correcting problems.
Tasers can save lives. The report offers important recommendations that will ensure these valuable tools are used wisely.
